system:
You audit the knowledge atoms of one Knowledge Card. A card is the answer key for a benchmark of expert conceptual knowledge, so every atom must be correct, self-contained, and assessable on its own.

Judge every atom on every check listed below. Rules:
- For checks about evidence, use only the evidence sentences supplied with the atom. Do not repair an atom with your own knowledge.
- For GROUNDED, use "hold" when unreadable PDF symbols prevent verification; explain what is needed. Use fail only when the available evidence is sufficient to determine that the claim is unsupported. This hold rule takes precedence over the strictness rule. Judge other checks independently using their listed values; do not invent missing facts.
- Be strict within each check's allowed values. Do not turn an inability to verify GROUNDED into revise or fail; use hold as defined above.
- "why" is required for every value other than the first listed value; keep it under 30 words. Omit "why" when passing.

Checks (allowed values in brackets; the first value means no problem):
- GROUNDED [pass / revise / fail / hold]: The cited evidence sentences state the atom, including its specificity, causal force, assumptions, and certainty. pass = fully stated. revise = partly stated (the atom adds, drops, or strengthens something; say what). fail = not stated when the available evidence permits a judgment. hold = unreadable symbols prevent verification. For pass or revise, put the supporting evidence ids in cite.
- SINGLE_CLAIM [pass / revise]: The atom is one independently assessable claim. revise = it joins two or more claims that could be true or false separately. Evidence spanning more than three sentences is not by itself a reason to split or revise an atom.
- SCOPE_LABEL [pass / revise]: The S label fits (S1 what it is / S2 how it works / S3 where it ends). revise = wrong label; put the right one in why, e.g. 'S2: ...'.
- L1_ONLY [pass / fail]: The atom is recall-level knowledge. fail = knowing it requires applying the concept to a new problem, or combining facts from distant passages.
- SOURCE_INDEPENDENT [pass / revise / fail]: A domain expert who never read this book could judge the claim true or false. revise = phrased as the authors' statement but the claim itself is general (drop the attribution). fail = an isolated study finding, conjecture, or author-specific opinion, classification, or recommendation, even if attribution was removed. Explicitly scoped established facts about a formalism or architecture and conditional theoretical results remain eligible.
- NO_OVERLAP [pass / fail]: No other atom in this card states or contains the same claim. If two atoms overlap, fail only the less informative one and put the other atom's id in cite; the other one passes.
- CENTRALITY [pass / fail]: The atom matters for understanding the concept. fail = peripheral detail.
Whole-card checks (report under "batch"):
- CONCEPT_SCOPE [pass / fail]: The concept is a general concept of the field. fail = a topic whose assessable content is restricted to excluded study-specific findings or author-specific positions. A named formalism, system, or architecture is not disqualified solely for being specific if its scoped conceptual facts are source-independent.

Output ONLY one JSON object:
{"units": {"<atom_id>": {"<CHECK>": {"v": "<value>", "why": "", "cite": []}, ...}, ...}, "batch": {"<CHECK>": {"v": "<value>", "why": ""}}}

CONCEPT: Zig-zag product
ASSESSMENT SCOPE: Replacement and zig-zag graph products, the expansion (second-eigenvalue) analysis, and how Reingold's iterated construction yields deterministic O(log n)-memory graph exploration. Excludes the bibliographic remarks on alternative proofs.

ATOMS:
- CS-ALG-C01-S1-01 | S1
  ATOM: The zig-zag product $G \,\textcircled{z}\, H$ has the same vertex set as the replacement product $G \,\textcircled{r}\, H$, but it contains only edges between clouds of different vertices.
  EVIDENCE:
    [CS-ALG-p0170-s19] The zig-zag-product Gz⃝H has the same set of vertices as the replacement product Gr⃝H, but only edges between vertex clouds of different vertices.
- CS-ALG-C01-S1-02 | S1
  ATOM: The replacement product $G \mathbin{r} H$ of a fully $d$-regular graph $G$ with a $c$-regular graph $H$ on $d$ vertices replaces each vertex of $G$ by a copy of $H$ (its cloud). Edges within a cloud keep their colors from $H$, and each edge of $G$ becomes an edge of a new inter-cloud color between the corresponding clouds.
  EVIDENCE:
    [CS-ALG-p0170-s12] Let G be a fully d-regular graph with n vertices and let H be a c-regular graph with d vertices where c and d are constants.
    [CS-ALG-p0170-s13] Then the replace- ment product Gr⃝H is the graph where each vertex v in G is replaced by a copy of H that we call the cloud of v.
    [CS-ALG-p0170-s14] The edges within a cloud keep the colors that they have in H.
    [CS-ALG-p0170-s15] For each edge of G, we introduce an edge with a new inter-cloud color between the respective vertices in the corresponding clouds; cf.
- CS-ALG-C01-S1-03 | S1
  ATOM: Every edge of the zig-zag product $G \mathbin{z} H$ corresponds to a path of length three in the replacement product $G \mathbin{r} H$ whose middle edge is an inter-cloud edge.
  EVIDENCE:
    [CS-ALG-p0171-s06] Every edge in G z⃝H corresponds to a path of length three in Gr⃝H where the middle edge is purple, e.g.,an edge color gold in Gz⃝H corresponds to a path in Gr⃝H that is teal-pink-brown.
- CS-ALG-C01-S2-01 | S2
  ATOM: A traversal sequence for $G_i$ can be turned into one for $G_{i-1}$ with constant memory overhead, because the step takes a zig-zag product with a constant-size graph and an 8th power. Over $\ell = O(\log n)$ levels this gives an exploration sequence for G with memory overhead $O(\ell)=O(\log n)$.
  EVIDENCE:
    [CS-ALG-p0172-s14] Any traversal sequence for Gi can be transformed with constant memory overhead to a traversal sequence for Gi−1, since it involves taking the zig-zag product with a graph of constant size and power 8 (which requires to memorize up to 7 additional steps).
    [CS-ALG-p0172-s15] Thus, a traversal sequence for Gℓcan be transformed to a traversal sequence for G0 and, hence, an exploration sequence for G with memory overhead of O (ℓ) = O (logn).
- CS-ALG-C01-S2-02 | S2
  ATOM: In Reingold's iterated construction, $G_i=(G_{i-1}\,\textcircled{z}\,H)^8$ satisfies $\lambda(G_i)\le\max\{\lambda(G_{i-1})^2,1/2\}$ for all $i=1,\dots,\ell$.
  EVIDENCE:
    [CS-ALG-p0172-s12] For i = 1,...,ℓ, deﬁne Gi = (Gi−1 z⃝H)8, i.e.,to obtain the next graph in the sequence, we ﬁrst apply the zig-zag product with H and then take the 8-th power of the resulting graph.
    [CS-ALG-p0172-s17] We claim that λ(Gi) ≤max{λ(Gi−1)2,1/2} for all i = 1,...,ℓ.
- CS-ALG-C01-S2-03 | S2
  ATOM: If $G$ is an $(n,d,\lambda)$-graph and $H$ is a $(d,c,1/2)$-graph, then $G\,\textcircled{z}\,H$ is an $\left(nd,\,c^2,\,\tfrac18\left(3\lambda+\sqrt{9\lambda^2+16}\right)\right)$-graph.
  EVIDENCE:
    [CS-ALG-p0172-s06] Reingold et al. [17]: Let G be an (n,d,λ)-graph and let H be a (d,c,1/2)-graph.
    [CS-ALG-p0172-s07] Then Gz⃝H is an √ nd,c2, 18(3λ + 9λ2 +16) -graph.
- CS-ALG-C01-S3-01 | S3
  ATOM: The zig-zag construction also works when $G$ has bi-colored edges, provided inter-cloud edges are allowed between different copies of vertices of $H$. The resulting $G\,\textcircled{z}\,H$ may still have bi-colored edges.
  EVIDENCE:
    [CS-ALG-p0170-s24] We note that this construction also works if G has bi- colored edges by allowing inter-cloud edges also between different copies of vertices of H.
    [CS-ALG-p0170-s25] In any case, we may end up with a graph Gz⃝H having bi-colored edges.
- CS-ALG-C01-S3-02 | S3
  ATOM: The zig-zag product of $G_{i-1}$ with H is well defined in the iteration because the zig-zag product has degree $c^2$ and the 8th power of the zig-zag product has degree $c^{16}$. $G_i$ therefore has degree $c^{16}$, which matches the number of vertices of H.
  EVIDENCE:
    [CS-ALG-p0172-s13] Note that this is well-deﬁned since Gi−1 z⃝H has degree c2, so that Gi = (Gi−1 z⃝H)8 has degree c16, and Gi z⃝H is deﬁned.
- CS-ALG-C01-S3-03 | S3
  ATOM: If $G$ has bi-colored edges, the zig-zag product still works by allowing inter-cloud edges between different copies of vertices of $H$, but the resulting graph $G \,\textcircled{z}\, H$ may still have bi-colored edges.
  EVIDENCE:
    [CS-ALG-p0170-s24] We note that this construction also works if G has bi- colored edges by allowing inter-cloud edges also between different copies of vertices of H.
    [CS-ALG-p0170-s25] In any case, we may end up with a graph Gz⃝H having bi-colored edges.
- CS-ALG-C01-S3-04 | S3
  ATOM: The zig-zag product construction also works when G has bi-colored edges, provided inter-cloud edges are allowed between different copies of vertices of H. The resulting product may itself still have bi-colored edges.
  EVIDENCE:
    [CS-ALG-p0170-s24] We note that this construction also works if G has bi- colored edges by allowing inter-cloud edges also between different copies of vertices of H.
    [CS-ALG-p0170-s25] In any case, we may end up with a graph Gz⃝H having bi-colored edges.
